answer: Ongoing monitoring evaluates the extent to which a model continues to perform as expected given potential changes in products, exposures, activities, clients, data relevance, or market conditions, and the frequency and scope of monitoring reports depend on the nature of the model and its materiality [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].### Quantities, frequencies, and boundsThe monitoring program should re-report the same quantities this validation checked, against the same declared bounds, so that a production reading is directly comparable to the validation reading rather than to a separately invented target.Rank-ordering on scored production cohorts should be tracked each quarter, once outcomes for the performance window have matured, against a floor of 0.7 [[art:8bfd02cc:threshold.package.auc.test.min]], with the validation reading of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] as the reference point for trend analysis.Mean squared probability error should be tracked on the same quarterly cycle against a ceiling of 0.2 [[art:d0f98b9c:threshold.package.brier.test.max]], with the validation reading of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] as its reference point.The regression of realized outcomes on the log-odds of the predicted probability should be refitted each quarter and held inside the declared band running from 0.8 [[art:95fdb848:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.min]] to 1.2 [[art:0adb7a89:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.max]], against a validation reading of 1.003 [[art:b7dbb687:calibration_slope.test]] that sits near the centre of that band and therefore leaves little headroom to be spent before drift becomes visible.Population stability of the scored inputs and of the score itself should be measured monthly, since it needs no outcome data and is the earliest available warning, against a ceiling of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]].The train-to-test comparison in this validation reached only 0.01095 [[art:381b2570:psi.max]] at its largest, so the operative signal in production is not proximity to the ceiling but movement away from that near-zero baseline, and a materially raised monthly reading should trigger investigation well before the declared bound is approached.Each monthly and quarterly report should carry the reading, the bound it is measured against, and the direction and size of the movement since the prior period, rather than a pass indicator alone.### Ordering of the monitoring reportFor any future cohort whose observed event rate falls below 0.05 [[art:42f1351e:rule.calibration_first_event_rate]], the monitoring report for that cohort should lead with calibration and place discrimination after it, because at low event rates the absolute level of the predicted probabilities is the more fragile property and the one that drives downstream use.When the observed rate for a cohort sits at or above that bound, the monitoring report should retain the ordering used in this validation.The observed event rate of each monitored cohort should therefore be reported explicitly alongside the metrics, since it determines how the report is to be read.### Benchmarking that monitoring addsSection 2 of this report compares the champion against a challenger fitted on the same development data, and that comparison is bounded by the fact that both models see the same historical sample.Monitoring should add two comparisons that the development data cannot supply.The first is a benchmark against an external reference, specifically a vendor or bureau credit score obtained on the same production cohorts, compared on rank-ordering and on realized default rates by score band; discrepancies should trigger investigation into their source and magnitude, and agreement should be read as supporting evidence rather than as assurance [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.b]].The second is a periodic refit of the challenger on production vintages, run in parallel against realized outcomes, so that a persistent advantage for the refitted challenger over the deployed champion can be detected and read as a signal that adjustment, recalibration, or redevelopment may be warranted [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.b]].These two comparisons answer different questions and neither substitutes for the other: the external reference tests whether the champion is competitive against information the organisation does not itself produce, while the refitted challenger tests whether the champion's fitted structure has aged relative to current data.### What monitoring must watch that this validation could notThis validation observed the model on a held-out split of the development sample, which is a static snapshot; it cannot speak to the passage of time, and the items below therefore fall to monitoring.- Out-of-time behaviour on cohorts booked after the development window, including any shift in the applicant mix arising from changes in products, exposures, or client base, which is exactly the class of change ongoing monitoring is directed at [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].- Realized outcomes over the full performance window, through back-testing on periods not used in development, supplemented by early-warning metrics reported shortly after deployment while the longer window is still accumulating.- Macroeconomic and credit-cycle conditions outside the range represented in the development sample, with attention to situations where the input ranges the model was fitted over are approached or exceeded.- Overrides of the model's output by users, tracked with their stated reasons and their subsequent performance, since a high override rate or overrides that consistently improve on the model would indicate the model is not performing as intended.- Implementation and process verification in the production environment, covering the accuracy and completeness of the live data feeds, the equivalence of the production scoring path to the scored artefact examined here, and change control over the deployed code.- The behaviour of the score on population segments as their composition shifts, since a stable aggregate reading can conceal offsetting movement between segments.A breach of any declared bound, or a persistent one-directional drift within a bound, should invoke the organisation's escalation path and prompt consideration of overlays, adjustment, recalibration, or redevelopment [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].The monitoring plan should itself be revisited at each periodic revalidation, so that the bounds and frequencies recommended here are reassessed against accumulated production experience rather than carried forward unexamined.
judge_rationale: All five hold; every number cited, matched, no names or absence claims.

answer: Validating conceptual soundness means assessing and documenting the model's design, its key modeling choices and assumptions, its construction, and the developmental evidence behind it, and subjecting those aspects to critical analysis rather than accepting them as documented [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].### Design and input timingThe champion is a linear logistic scorecard: a single linear index with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] and one coefficient per retained feature, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows and scored as a default probability.The declared feature set contains 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts and 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are fixed at origination.None are declared as observed during the performance period, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none as observed after the outcome, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]].On the timing declaration alone, then, every input is available at the moment the score would be used, which is what a forward-looking application scorecard requires; the declaration is the developer's own labelling, and this section takes it as design evidence rather than as an independent test of it.### The developer's own screenThe model's collinearity screen was run at a variance-inflation threshold of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]] and removed two of the declared features before fitting.The last bill amount was removed at a variance inflation of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], far above that threshold, which is what one expects of a level that is nearly reconstructible from the retained six-month bill mean and bill trend.The six-month mean utilisation was removed at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], again above the threshold and again close to a retained feature, the point-in-time utilisation.Both removals are the kind of judgment this design should make: the screen drops the redundant member of each pair and keeps a spanning set, and it is documented with the diagnostic that motivated it.### Fitted coefficients and expected signsThe largest coefficient in the fitted index is on the most recent delinquency status, at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], and its positive direction is what credit subject matter expects: a customer currently behind is more likely to default.The next largest are the six-month bill mean at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]] and the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], the latter in the expected direction, since a customer who has been paying down a larger share of each statement is the better risk.Utilisation enters at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], positive as expected, and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].The remaining coefficients are smaller: the delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the latest payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month maximum delinquency at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].The negative sign on the six-month bill mean is worth flagging in words: a scorecard user would not read a higher average statement balance as protective on its own, and the sign is defensible only as a conditional effect once utilisation and the bill trend are in the index.### Sign agreement and how much each disagreement mattersThe sign evidence compares each fitted coefficient's direction with the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with the outcome on train, and 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the retained features disagree.These comparisons and the refit deltas below are developmental evidence for the judgement in this section, not tests against a bound, and nothing in them is reported here as a finding.Each refit delta is measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature, which reaches a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]], so a negative delta means the feature was carrying discrimination and a positive delta means the refit without it scored slightly higher.The credit limit is the first disagreement: its fitted sign is +1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], recorded as disagreeing at 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]].On its own a larger limit goes with lower default risk, as the univariate direction says and as an underwriter would expect, so the positive fitted coefficient runs against subject matter; dropping the feature moves test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], so the model leans on it barely at all and the flip carries little consequence for the score.The latest payment ratio is the second: fitted sign +1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], disagreeing at 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].This is the more interesting of the small disagreements, because the six-month mean of the same quantity enters with the expected negative sign, so the positive coefficient on the point-in-time version reads as a within-pair partialling effect rather than as a claim that paying more this month raises risk.Refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again a feature the model does not depend on.The six-month maximum delinquency is the third: fitted sign -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of +1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], disagreeing at 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].A negative coefficient on a worst-delinquency measure is counter-intuitive on its face, and here too the natural reading is collinearity with the current delinquency status and the delinquency count, both of which enter positively; the refit without it moves test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest reliance of the three.The two features the model actually depends on both agree with their univariate directions, which is the more important fact for interpretability.The current delinquency status agrees at 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]], with fitted sign +1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]] and univariate direction +1 [[art:a78648ba:sign_check.delinq_last.univariate_direction]], and removing it costs -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC, by far the largest reliance in the model.Utilisation agrees at 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]], with fitted sign +1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]] and univariate direction +1 [[art:f0995196:sign_check.utilisation.univariate_direction]], and removing it costs -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]].The six-month bill mean also agrees at 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]], with fitted sign -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]] matching a univariate direction of -1 [[art:23b89c5d:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], and it carries a modest amount of discrimination, -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].Age, the six-month mean payment ratio, the bill trend and the delinquency count all agree as well, at 1 [[art:4116add1:sign_check.age.agrees]], 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]], 1 [[art:ff3cb24a:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.agrees]] and 1 [[art:a337d16b:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.agrees]] respectively, with the payment-ratio mean fitted negative at -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:24dcef24:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.univariate_direction]], age negative at -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:66364583:sign_check.age.univariate_direction]], the bill trend negative at -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]] against -1 [[art:a9bff389:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.univariate_direction]], and the delinquency count positive at 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]] against 1 [[art:549e904e:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.univariate_direction]].Several of the agreeing features nonetheless contribute nothing the rest of the index does not already carry, since refits without them score slightly higher: 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]] for the payment-ratio mean, 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]] for the bill trend, 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]] for the delinquency count, and 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]] for age.Taken together, the design is a thin model in practice: discrimination is concentrated in the delinquency status and utilisation, and the remaining eight coefficients are close to free parameters whose signs should not be read as behavioural statements.### Effective challengeThe champion scores a test AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].A histogram gradient-boosting challenger, fitted as the alternative methodology for this comparison, reaches a test AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]], so it is both better ordered and better calibrated on the same test data.The lead is 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]] of AUC, read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]] that decides whether such a difference is material, and it exceeds that threshold by more than double.This is raised as a finding on effective challenge, and because the challenger differs from the champion chiefly in functional form, the finding is in substance about the champion's functional form: a linear index in these features leaves a material amount of the available discrimination unused, most plausibly non-linearity and interaction among the delinquency and utilisation measures.That finding, its severity and its disposition are reported in the findings section, which is where the reader should go for it.The more general judgement of this section is that the design is defensible in its inputs, its timing and its collinearity screen, that its coefficient signs are interpretable except for three small-reliance disagreements described above, and that its choice of functional form is where the effective-challenge evidence pushes back hardest.

answer: Validating conceptual soundness means assessing and documenting the model's design — its key modelling choices, assumptions, qualitative judgments and data selection — together with its construction and developmental testing, and this section does that for the credit_default champion by examining its inputs, its fitted coefficients, and its performance against a challenger. [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]]### Design and inputsThe champion is a single linear scoring model in the log-odds, carrying one fitted coefficient per retained feature plus an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], estimated on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows.The declared feature set has 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] members, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period opens.The count of inputs first observable inside the performance window is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]] and the count observable only after the outcome is 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the timing evidence every input is available at the moment the score would be used and none of them can carry the outcome back into the score.That is the right shape for a forward-looking default score, and it is the single most important design property to have established before any of the performance numbers are read.The developer's own collinearity screen dropped two inputs before fitting.It removed bill_last, whose variance inflation was 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and utilisation_mean_6m, at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both read against the screen's own cut of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].Both removals are defensible on their face: a point-in-time bill level is close to redundant against the averaged bill level over the recent window, and an averaged utilisation is close to redundant against point-in-time utilisation, so retaining them would have destabilised the surviving coefficients without adding much that the retained pair does not already carry.The consequence for interpretation is that the retained bill and utilisation coefficients absorb the influence of their dropped partners, and should be read as the effect of a bill-level block and a utilisation block rather than of narrowly separable quantities.### Coefficients and expected directionThe largest coefficient by magnitude sits on delinq_last at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], well clear of the rest of the vector.Behind it come bill_mean_6m at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], pay_ratio_mean_6m at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]], and bill_trend_6m at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].The remainder are an order of magnitude smaller in influence: delinq_count_6m at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], pay_ratio_last at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], limit_bal at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and delinq_max_6m at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].Credit subject matter expects recent delinquency and high utilisation to raise default risk, and stronger repayment behaviour to lower it.The model's dominant terms match that expectation: the sign on delinq_last is positive, 1 [[art:50d352f8:sign_check.delinq_last.coef_sign]], the sign on utilisation is positive, 1 [[art:85badc3c:sign_check.utilisation.coef_sign]], and the sign on the averaged payment ratio is negative, -1 [[art:077bb6b2:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.coef_sign]].The negative sign on the averaged bill level, -1 [[art:cee1a18f:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.coef_sign]], and on the bill trend, -1 [[art:7fd8474e:sign_check.bill_trend_6m.coef_sign]], is less immediately intuitive but is consistent with a large and rising billed balance marking an active, well-served account rather than a distressed one, and each of these agrees with its own univariate direction.The negative sign on age, -1 [[art:6172eb93:sign_check.age.coef_sign]], and the positive sign on the delinquency count, 1 [[art:17afb6f9:sign_check.delinq_count_6m.coef_sign]], are also as the subject matter would predict.### Sign agreement and per-feature contributionThe comparison between each fitted sign and the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with the outcome on train, and the change in test AUC when the champion's form is refitted without a feature, are evidence supporting the judgement in this section rather than the subject of any rule, and nothing described in this subsection is a finding.The ablation deltas are measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature, which reaches 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] on test.On the sign comparison, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] retained features carry a fitted sign that contradicts their own univariate direction, and each is set out below with the discrimination it carries.The fitted sign on limit_bal is positive, 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]], while its own univariate direction is negative, -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], so the two disagree, 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]].Refitting without limit_bal changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement rather than a loss, so the model is not leaning on the feature and the flipped sign is a presentational rather than a predictive concern.The fitted sign on pay_ratio_last is positive, 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]], against a negative univariate direction, -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], and the two disagree, 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]].This is the sharper of the three to explain, because the averaged payment ratio in the same model keeps the expected negative sign, so the point-in-time term is reading as a residual against that average rather than as a level effect.Refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again an improvement, so the contradiction sits on a term the model does not depend on.The fitted sign on delinq_max_6m is negative, -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]], against a positive univariate direction, 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], and the two disagree, 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]].The most likely reading is collinearity within the delinquency block, where the recent delinquency marker and the delinquency count already carry the risk signal and the maximum term takes a small offsetting weight.Removing it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest contribution of the three disagreeing features, so the sign flip is on a term of negligible predictive weight.By contrast, the features the champion actually depends on are the ones whose signs agree with their univariate direction.Refitting without delinq_last costs -0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC and refitting without utilisation costs -0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], so almost all of the champion's discrimination rests on those two, both of which point in the direction the subject matter expects.The averaged bill level also contributes, at -0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]], and its sign agrees with its univariate direction as well.The remaining terms do not pay for themselves on test: dropping age changes AUC by 8.675e-05 [[art:59398b1b:ablation.age.delta_auc]], dropping the delinquency count by 0.0006812 [[art:c5659def:ablation.delinq_count_6m.delta_auc]], dropping the bill trend by 0.003279 [[art:096d7f98:ablation.bill_trend_6m.delta_auc]], and dropping the averaged payment ratio by 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], each an increase.That last one deserves comment: the averaged payment ratio carries one of the larger coefficients and a sign the subject matter endorses, yet the fit is measurably better on test without it, which points to the linear form spending weight on a term whose contribution does not generalise.Taken together, the picture is a model whose economically central terms are sound and whose periphery is over-specified, with a handful of small coefficients absorbing collinear residual structure and carrying the sign disagreements with them.### Effective challengeThe champion reaches an AUC of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] on test with a Brier score of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].A histogram gradient boosting challenger, fitted for comparison on the same retained inputs, reaches an AUC of 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] with a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]], better on both discrimination and calibration-sensitive accuracy.The challenger's lead over the champion is 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], read against an effective-challenge threshold of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], which it exceeds by a wide margin.That gap is finding E1.E1 is a finding about the champion's functional form, and this section flags it as such.The challenger sees the same inputs at the same timing and differs from the champion principally in that it can represent non-linearity and interaction among the delinquency, utilisation and billing blocks, which a single linear index cannot; the size of the gap is therefore evidence that the linear specification, not the feature set, is what limits the champion.The over-specified periphery documented above points the same way, since a form that must express every effect as a constant log-odds slope will spend weight on terms that do not generalise.The findings section reports E1, its severity and its disposition, and this section does not restate them.### JudgementOn design, the champion is transparent, its inputs are all knowable before the performance window opens, and its collinearity screen is justified on the evidence presented.On direction, the terms that carry the model's discrimination behave as the subject matter expects, and the sign disagreements fall on terms whose removal does not cost the model anything measurable on test.The substantive reservation from this section is the functional form, which the effective-challenge comparison addresses and which is carried into the findings section as E1; the sign disagreements and the negative-contribution terms are recorded here as design observations for the developer to address at the next refit.

[[reg:SR26-2:IV.1]]### 3.1 Split sizes and missingnessThe training split holds 3500 [[art:2510d49d:profile.train.n]] rows and the test split holds 1500 [[art:2193cf5f:profile.test.n]] rows.The largest [[art:f813848d:profile.test.missing.max]].Because both splits are fully populated, the difference in missingness between them is nil and leaves the tolerated between-split gap of 0.1 [[art:9cce25ea:threshold.D1.missing_gap]] unapproached.No imputation behaviour therefore differs between the split the model learned on and the split it was scored on, which removes one common route by which a holdout can flatter a model.### 3.2 Population and characteristic stabilityThe largest population stability index measured from the training split against the test split, with the score included among the measured quantities, is 0.01095 [[art:381b2570:psi.max]], against a bound of 0.25 [[art:278b9016:threshold.S1.psi]].The package declares the same stability ceiling of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]], so the declared and applied bounds agree and no reconciliation between them is needed.The train-to-test population stability index for each measured quantity is as follows.- Credit limit: 0.01095 [[art:601cdba2:psi.limit_bal]]- Bill trend over six months: 0.00958 [[art:c247a6f2:psi.bill_trend_6m]]- Age: 0.008124 [[art:f9255a0a:psi.age]]- Mean bill over six months: 0.007124 [[art:028e4281:psi.bill_mean_6m]]- Model score: 0.007023 [[art:a2885abf:psi.y_score]]- Maximum delinquency over six months: 0.005498 [[art:7a82e7f3:psi.delinq_max_6m]]- Mean payment ratio over six months: 0.0055 [[art:2c5baeb2:psi.pay_ratio_mean_6m]]- Last payment ratio: 0.004966 [[art:3af2ca29:psi.pay_ratio_last]]- Utilisation: 0.004244 [[art:451e0780:psi.utilisation]]- Last delinquency: 0.00285 [[art:03bd52e7:psi.delinq_last]]- Delinquency count over six months: 0.002069 [[art:61491d02:psi.delinq_count_6m]]The credit limit is the least stable of these quantities, and even it sits more than an order of magnitude inside the bound of 0.25 [[art:278b9016:threshold.S1.psi]].That the score's own shift, at 0.007023 [[art:a2885abf:psi.y_score]], is of the same small order as the inputs is consistent with a scoring function that is not amplifying input movement.At the characteristic level, the largest single contribution to the shift in the linear predictor is 0.02363 [[art:e56cb179:csi.max]], which is attributable to the last delinquency indicator at 0.02363 [[art:5babe364:csi.delinq_last]].Read against the declared stability ceiling of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]], that contribution is an order of magnitude inside the bound.The per-characteristic contributions are as follows.- Last delinquency: 0.02363 [[art:5babe364:csi.delinq_last]]- Bill trend over six months: 0.00633 [[art:59948e6d:csi.bill_trend_6m]]- Utilisation: 0.004042 [[art:10f0f9e7:csi.utilisation]]- Delinquency count over six months: 0.002449 [[art:69346f52:csi.delinq_count_6m]]- Mean bill over six months: 0.002369 [[art:48df6cc9:csi.bill_mean_6m]]- Last payment ratio: 0.001924 [[art:aff2b4bf:csi.pay_ratio_last]]- Mean payment months: 0.0008965 [[art:7244960d:csi.delinq_max_6m]]The ordering of characteristic contributions differs from the ordering of marginal population shifts, since the last delinquency indicator moves little on its own but carries weight in the predictor, while the credit limit moves most but carries little weight.Neither view puts the training split materially out of line with the test split.### 3.3 Leakage screensFour independent screens were run for leakage, and each is reported against its own bound below.On declared feature timing, the number of features declared as observed during the performance period or after the outcome is 0 [[art:742bcd24:leakage.timing.n_flagged]], so no feature is declared to be observable only at or after the point the target is known.This screen rests on the declared timings themselves, so it is only as strong as the accuracy of those declarations; it does not detect a feature whose timing is mis-declared.On predictive strength, the area under the pattern.The contamination screen has two arms, and each is read against its own bound.The share of test rows whose identifier also identifies a row of the training split is 0 [[art:63d37fc5:leakage.overlap.ids]], against the declared bound of 0.005 [[art:9f336eaf:threshold.L2.overlap]].The share of test rows whose feature vector also appears in the training split is 0 [[art:0fec8048:leakage.overlap.features]], against the bound the feature-overlap arm actually applied, 0.005 [[art:1ee888c5:threshold.L2.overlap.features_effective]].That effective bound is the larger of the declared overlap bound and twice the within-train duplicate share, which is 0 [[art:4474c227:leakage.duplicates.train]], because two different subjects recording the same discrete row is coincidence rather than contamination; with no duplicate rows inside the training split, the effective bound reduces to the declared one.Both arms return exactly zero, so the two bounds are not distinguished by the outcome here, and the distinction would only matter on a dataset with coarse or repeated feature vectors.On feature naming, the number of feature names matching the target-adjacent lexicon is 0 [[art:407e62be:leakage.name_screen.n_matched]], so no input is named in a way that suggests it encodes the outcome.This is a lexical screen and would not catch a leaking feature under an innocuous name, so it supports rather than substitutes for the timing and predictive-strength screens above.### 3.4 AssessmentOn the evidence in this section, the two splits are alike in missingness, alike in the distribution of every measured input and of the score, and free of identifier or feature-vector contamination at the bounds each arm applied.The residual weakness is one of construction rather than of measurement: the timing and naming screens depend on declared metadata, so their reassurance is conditional on those declarations being correct, and stability measured between two splits of one extraction speaks to the split procedure rather than to how the population will move after deployment.Ongoing monitoring of the same stability quantities against live data would be needed before the low shifts recorded here could be read as evidence about post-deployment behaviour.

question: Section: monitoring. Grade the drafted prose against the grounding rubric.

answer: Ongoing monitoring evaluates the extent to which a model continues to perform as expected given potential changes in products, exposures, activities, clients, data relevance, or market conditions, and the frequency and scope of monitoring reports depend on the nature of the model and its materiality [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].### Quantities, frequencies, and boundsThe monitoring program should re-report the same quantities this validation checked, against the same declared bounds, so that a production reading is directly comparable to the validation reading rather than to a separately invented target.Rank-ordering on scored production cohorts should be tracked each quarter, once outcomes for the performance window have matured, against a floor of 0.7 [[art:8bfd02cc:threshold.package.auc.test.min]], with the validation reading of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] as the reference point for trend analysis.Mean squared probability error should be tracked on the same quarterly cycle against a ceiling of 0.2 [[art:d0f98b9c:threshold.package.brier.test.max]], with the validation reading of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] as its reference point.The regression of realized outcomes on the log-odds of the predicted probability should be refitted each quarter and held inside the declared band running from 0.8 [[art:95fdb848:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.min]] to 1.2 [[art:0adb7a89:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.max]], against a validation reading of 1.003 [[art:b7dbb687:calibration_slope.test]] that sits near the centre of that band and therefore leaves little headroom to be spent before drift becomes visible.Population stability of the scored inputs and of the score itself should be measured monthly, since it needs no outcome data and is the earliest available warning, against a ceiling of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]].The train-to-test comparison in this validation reached only 0.01095 [[art:381b2570:psi.max]] at its largest, so the operative signal in production is not proximity to the ceiling but movement away from that near-zero baseline, and a materially raised monthly reading should trigger investigation well before the declared bound is approached.Each monthly and quarterly report should carry the reading, the bound it is measured against, and the direction and size of the movement since the prior period, rather than a pass indicator alone.### Ordering of the monitoring reportFor any future cohort whose observed event rate falls below 0.05 [[art:42f1351e:rule.calibration_first_event_rate]], the monitoring report for that cohort should lead with calibration and place discrimination after it, because at low event rates the absolute level of the predicted probabilities is the more fragile property and the one that drives downstream use.When the observed rate for a cohort sits at or above that bound, the monitoring report should retain the ordering used in this validation.The observed event rate of each monitored cohort should therefore be reported explicitly alongside the metrics, since it determines how the report is to be read.### Benchmarking that monitoring addsSection 2 of this report compares the champion against a challenger fitted on the same development data, and that comparison is bounded by the fact that both models see the same historical sample.Monitoring should add two comparisons that the development data cannot supply.The first is a benchmark against an external reference, specifically a vendor or bureau credit score obtained on the same production cohorts, compared on rank-ordering and on realized default rates by score band; discrepancies should trigger investigation into their source and magnitude, and agreement should be read as supporting evidence rather than as assurance [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.b]].The second is a periodic refit of the challenger on production vintages, run in parallel against realized outcomes, so that a persistent advantage for the refitted challenger over the deployed champion can be detected and read as a signal that adjustment, recalibration, or redevelopment may be warranted [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.b]].These two comparisons answer different questions and neither substitutes for the other: the external reference tests whether the champion is competitive against information the organisation does not itself produce, while the refitted challenger tests whether the champion's fitted structure has aged relative to current data.### What monitoring must watch that this validation could notThis validation observed the model on a held-out split of the development sample, which is a static snapshot; it cannot speak to the passage of time, and the items below therefore fall to monitoring.- Out-of-time behaviour on cohorts booked after the development window, including any shift in the applicant mix arising from changes in products, exposures, or client base, which is exactly the class of change ongoing monitoring is directed at [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].- Realized outcomes over the full performance window, through back-testing on periods not used in development, supplemented by early-warning metrics reported shortly after deployment while the longer window is still accumulating.- Macroeconomic and credit-cycle conditions outside the range represented in the development sample, with attention to situations where the input ranges the model was fitted over are approached or exceeded.- Overrides of the model's output by users, tracked with their stated reasons and their subsequent performance, since a high override rate or overrides that consistently improve on the model would indicate the model is not performing as intended.- Implementation and process verification in the production environment, covering the accuracy and completeness of the live data feeds, the equivalence of the production scoring path to the scored artefact examined here, and change control over the deployed code.- The behaviour of the score on population segments as their composition shifts, since a stable aggregate reading can conceal offsetting movement between segments.A breach of any declared bound, or a persistent one-directional drift within a bound, should invoke the organisation's escalation path and prompt consideration of overlays, adjustment, recalibration, or redevelopment [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].The monitoring plan should itself be revisited at each periodic revalidation, so that the bounds and frequencies recommended here are reassessed against accumulated production experience rather than carried forward unexamined.
judge_rationale: All numbers cited, resolve, match values; no names or missing-quantity claims.

answer: Sensitivity analysis checks the impact of small changes in inputs and parameter values on model outputs, and stress testing across a wide range of inputs — including extreme values — helps establish the boundaries within which the model is stable [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.a]].### Multicollinearity among the retained featuresThe largest variance inflation factor across the retained features is 7.295 [[art:9ae7c45b:vif.max]], which sits below the review threshold of 10 [[art:aeb4f33c:threshold.M1.vif]].The individual values are 1.002 [[art:74c06cad:vif.age]] for age, 1.201 [[art:9356a256:vif.bill_trend_6m]] for the six-month bill trend, 1.412 [[art:48733638:vif.delinq_last]] for the most recent delinquency indicator, 2.408 [[art:71aaaf11:vif.delinq_max_6m]] for the six-month maximum delinquency, 2.561 [[art:38974def:vif.delinq_count_6m]] for the six-month delinquency count, 3.215 [[art:536fdb6f:vif.utilisation]] for utilisation, 4.803 [[art:ddfdcc3c:vif.limit_bal]] for the credit limit, 7.259 [[art:e39c3e82:vif.pay_ratio_mean_6m]] for the six-month mean payment ratio, 7.264 [[art:c2de8dfe:vif.pay_ratio_last]] for the most recent payment ratio, and 7.295 [[art:f0a2f865:vif.bill_mean_6m]] for the six-month mean bill amount, each measured on the training sample.The three largest of these sit close to one another and all attach to features built from the same six-month billing and payment history, so what collinearity remains is concentrated in that block rather than spread evenly across the design.Belsley's condition number of the column-standardised design is 5.547 [[art:e41b9562:condition_number]], against a threshold of 30 [[art:7e52fd7a:threshold.M1.condition_number]], so the design matrix is well conditioned and the coefficient estimates are not near-degenerate in the direction that a high condition number would signal.Taken together, the two diagnostics agree: neither the feature-by-feature view nor the whole-design view puts this specification near the point where correlated inputs would make individual coefficients unstable, though the clustering noted above is worth carrying forward into ongoing monitoring since correlations among behavioural features can drift with the portfolio.### Analyses that do not apply to this model typeThe package declares no regime column for this subject, so stability of the model across declared regimes is not an analysis that applies here, and it is listed on that basis in Appendix D.This subject is not a hazard model, so the rate-shock scenarios do not apply to it either: no value change at the extreme shocks was produced, no shock curve exists to test for monotonicity, and there is no convexity to compare against the direction the package declares.Both of these are recorded in Appendix D as out of scope for this model type, and nothing in this section should be read as reporting a result from them.

particular model to check the impact of small changes in inputs and parameter values on model outputs, and that stability be checked over a wide range of inputs [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.a]].### 5.1 consequence of constructing several features from one underlying billing history, and it is a limitation on the interpretation of the individual coefficients rather than on the fitted scores.The to the rest of the design.Belsley's condition number of the column-standardised design is 5.547 [[art:e41b9562:condition_number]], against a threshold of 30 [[art:7e52fd7a:threshold.M1.condition_number]].The design matrix is therefore well conditioned as a whole, which is consistent with the pairwise picture: the collinearity present is concentrated in a small group of related features and is not severe enough to make the coefficient estimates numerically fragile.No remediation of the feature set is recommended on the evidence in this section, though the correlated billing and repayment features should be read as a block when coefficient signs or magnitudes are interpreted.### 5.2 Analyses that do not apply to this model typeStability across answer: Design is assessed here as validation of conceptual soundness: the modelling choices, the construction, and the developmental evidence behind them, with interpretability measures and benchmarking against alternative models used where an appeal to theoretical construction alone would not settle the question [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].### The champion and its inputsThe champion is a logistic regression for credit default, fitted with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]] on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows and carrying a linear coefficient for each retained feature.The feature inventory offered to the model holds 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features.Of these, 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.None are drawn from during the performance period, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none from after the outcome is known, at 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on the timing labels alone every input is available at the moment the score would be used.The model's own collinearity screen then dropped two of the inventory before fitting.The balance feature bill_last was dropped with a variance inflation factor of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]], and the averaged utilisation feature utilisation_mean_6m with 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]], both far above the screen's cutoff of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].Both removals are consistent with the reason such a screen exists: each dropped feature restates information already carried by a retained one, the last bill by the mean bill and the averaged utilisation by the point-in-time utilisation, and leaving them in would have made the surviving coefficients unstable rather than more informative.The screen's stated purpose is served, but it should be read as a variance-reduction device and not as evidence that the retained coefficients are individually interpretable.### Coefficients and expected signsThe model leans hardest on recent delinquency, whose coefficient of 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]] is the largest in the fit and positive, which is the direction credit subject matter expects: a borrower delinquent in the most recent month is more likely to default.The next largest are the mean bill over six months at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]] and the mean payment ratio over six months at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]].The negative sign on the payment ratio is what the subject matter expects, since a borrower who repays a larger share of the balance is the safer borrower.The negative sign on the mean bill is less intuitive at face value, because a larger outstanding balance is usually read as more exposure and more risk; here it is more naturally read as conditional on utilisation and the delinquency terms, where a high absolute bill on a high limit is not the same signal as a high bill on a small limit.Utilisation enters positively at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend negatively at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]], and the positive utilisation sign matches the expectation that borrowers pressed against their limit default more often.The smaller terms are the last payment ratio at 0.1026 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_last.value]], the six-month delinquency count at 0.1226 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_count_6m.value]], the credit limit at 0.07266 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.limit_bal.value]], age at -0.06726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.age.value]], and the six-month delinquency maximum at -0.03221 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_max_6m.value]].Of these, the positive delinquency count and the negative age term read as expected, while a positive coefficient on the credit limit and a negative one on the worst delinquency in six months both run against what the subject matter would predict, since larger limits are typically extended to stronger borrowers and a worse delinquency peak is worse news.### Sign checks and ablation as supporting evidenceThe sign checks and the ablation deltas below are evidence bearing on the judgement in this section rather than the subject of any rule, and nothing in this subsection is a finding.The fitted signs contradict the features' own univariate directions on train for 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] of the validation-time value of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] as the reference point from which deterioration is measured.Track the slope of the logistic regression of the realized outcome on the logit of the predicted probability against the declared band of 0.8 [[art:95fdb848:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.min]] to 1.2 [[art:0adb7a89:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.max]], with the validation-time value of 1.003 [[art:b7dbb687:calibration_slope.test]] as the reference point.Track mean squared error of the predicted probability against the outcome on each cohort against the declared ceiling of 0.2 [[art:d0f98b9c:threshold.package.brier.test.max]], with the validation-time value of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] as the reference point.Track the population stability index of each model input and of the score itself against the declared ceiling of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]], noting that the largest shift observed between the development and evaluation splits was 0.01095 [[art:381b2570:psi.max]].Because the observed shift sits far below the declared ceiling, monitoring should set an internal review trigger at a fraction of that ceiling rather than waiting for the declared bound to be reached, so that drift is investigated while it is still small.### FrequencyThe stability quantities and the input distributions depend only on scored records and should be produced each month, since they give the earliest warning of a shift and require no matured outcomes.Discrimination, the calibration slope, and the squared-error measure depend on realized defaults and should be produced each quarter, on cohorts whose performance window has closed, so that the comparison against the declared bounds is made on outcomes rather than on partial exposure.A fuller review that reconsiders the model's assumptions, its segment coverage, and the continued relevance of its development data is appropriate annually, or sooner if a monthly stability report or a quarterly outcomes report breaches its bound.### Ordering of the monitoring reportWhere a future monitoring cohort has an observed event rate below 0.05 [[art:42f1351e:rule.calibration_first_event_rate]], the report for that cohort should present calibration before discrimination, since rank-ordering statistics become unstable as events thin out and absolute probability accuracy carries the greater share of the decision.For cohorts at or above that rate, the ordering used in the discrimination and calibration section of this report remains appropriate.### BenchmarkingThe champion-versus-challenger comparison reported earlier in this validation is drawn entirely from the development and evaluation data, so it cannot speak to how either model behaves on vintages booked after the development window closed.Monitoring should add a benchmark that the development data cannot supply, namely the challenger refitted on production vintages and scored in parallel against the champion on the same matured cohorts, so that a persistent advantage for the refitted challenger surfaces as evidence that the champion's coefficients have aged.Where the alternative prediction is to come from outside the organization rather than from a refit, an external credit-bureau or vendor reference score is the appropriate second benchmark, and discrepancies against it should trigger investigation into their source and degree rather than being read as error in either model. [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.b]]

answer: Ongoing monitoring evaluates the extent to which a model continues to perform as expected given potential changes in products, exposures, activities, clients, data relevance, or market conditions, and the frequency and scope of monitoring reports depend on the nature of the model and its materiality [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].### Quantities, frequencies, and boundsThe monitoring program should re-report the same quantities this validation checked, against the same declared bounds, so that a production reading is directly comparable to the validation reading rather than to a separately invented target.Rank-ordering on scored production cohorts should be tracked each quarter, once outcomes for the performance window have matured, against a floor of 0.7 [[art:8bfd02cc:threshold.package.auc.test.min]], with the validation reading of 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] as the reference point for trend analysis.Mean squared probability error should be tracked on the same quarterly cycle against a ceiling of 0.2 [[art:d0f98b9c:threshold.package.brier.test.max]], with the validation reading of 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] as its reference point.The regression of realized outcomes on the log-odds of the predicted probability should be refitted each quarter and held inside the declared band running from 0.8 [[art:95fdb848:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.min]] to 1.2 [[art:0adb7a89:threshold.package.calibration_slope.test.max]], against a validation reading of 1.003 [[art:b7dbb687:calibration_slope.test]] that sits near the centre of that band and therefore leaves little headroom to be spent before drift becomes visible.Population stability of the scored inputs and of the score itself should be measured monthly, since it needs no outcome data and is the earliest available warning, against a ceiling of 0.25 [[art:fbb5a9d1:threshold.package.psi.max]].The train-to-test comparison in this validation reached only 0.01095 [[art:381b2570:psi.max]] at its largest, so the operative signal in production is not proximity to the ceiling but movement away from that near-zero baseline, and a materially raised monthly reading should trigger investigation well before the declared bound is approached.Each monthly and quarterly report should carry the reading, the bound it is measured against, and the direction and size of the movement since the prior period, rather than a pass indicator alone.### Ordering of the monitoring reportFor any future cohort whose observed event rate falls below 0.05 [[art:42f1351e:rule.calibration_first_event_rate]], the monitoring report for that cohort should lead with calibration and place discrimination after it, because at low event rates the absolute level of the predicted probabilities is the more fragile property and the one that drives downstream use.When the observed rate for a cohort sits at or above that bound, the monitoring report should retain the ordering used in this validation.The observed event rate of each monitored cohort should therefore be reported explicitly alongside the metrics, since it determines how the report is to be read.### Benchmarking that monitoring addsSection 2 of this report compares the champion against a challenger fitted on the same development data, and that comparison is bounded by the fact that both models see the same historical sample.Monitoring should add two comparisons that the development data cannot supply.The first is a benchmark against an external reference, specifically a vendor or bureau credit score obtained on the same production cohorts, compared on rank-ordering and on realized default rates by score band; discrepancies should trigger investigation into their source and magnitude, and agreement should be read as supporting evidence rather than as assurance [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.b]].The second is a periodic refit of the challenger on production vintages, run in parallel against realized outcomes, so that a persistent advantage for the refitted challenger over the deployed champion can be detected and read as a signal that adjustment, recalibration, or redevelopment may be warranted [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.b]].These two comparisons answer different questions and neither substitutes for the other: the external reference tests whether the champion is competitive against information the organisation does not itself produce, while the refitted challenger tests whether the champion's fitted structure has aged relative to current data.### What monitoring must watch that this validation could notThis validation observed the model on a held-out split of the development sample, which is a static snapshot; it cannot speak to the passage of time, and the items below therefore fall to monitoring.- Out-of-time behaviour on cohorts booked after the development window, including any shift in the applicant mix arising from changes in products, exposures, or client base, which is exactly the class of change ongoing monitoring is directed at [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].- Realized outcomes over the full performance window, through back-testing on periods not used in development, supplemented by early-warning metrics reported shortly after deployment while the longer window is still accumulating.- Macroeconomic and credit-cycle conditions outside the range represented in the development sample, with attention to situations where the input ranges the model was fitted over are approached or exceeded.- Overrides of the model's output by users, tracked with their stated reasons and their subsequent performance, since a high override rate or overrides that consistently improve on the model would indicate the model is not performing as intended.- Implementation and process verification in the production environment, covering the accuracy and completeness of the live data feeds, the equivalence of the production scoring path to the scored artefact examined here, and change control over the deployed code.- The behaviour of the score on population segments as their composition shifts, since a stable aggregate reading can conceal offsetting movement between segments.A breach of any declared bound, or a persistent one-directional drift within a bound, should invoke the organisation's escalation path and prompt consideration of overlays, adjustment, recalibration, or redevelopment [[reg:SR26-2:V.2]].The monitoring plan should itself be revisited at each periodic revalidation, so that the bounds and frequencies recommended here are reassessed against accumulated production experience rather than carried forward unexamined.
judge_rationale: All five hold; every number cited, matched, and no absent-quantity claims.

close behind it.The near-equality of those three values points to a shared billing-and-repayment block of correlated inputs rather than to one dominant redundancy between a single pair of features.The remaining retained features are lower: the credit limit at 4.803 [[art:ddfdcc3c:vif.limit_bal]], utilisation at 3.215 [[art:536fdb6f:vif.utilisation]], the six-month delinquency count at 2.561 [[art:38974def:vif.delinq_count_6m]], the six-month maximum delinquency at 2.408 [[art:71aaaf11:vif.delinq_max_6m]], the most recent delinquency indicator at 1.412 [[art:48733638:vif.delinq_last]], the six-month bill trend at 1.201 [[art:9356a256:vif.bill_trend_6m]], and age at 1.002 [[art:74c06cad:vif.age]].The condition number of the column-standardised design is 5.547 [[art:e41b9562:condition_number]], comfortably inside its threshold of 30 [[art:7e52fd7a:threshold.M1.condition_number]].The two diagnostics agree: neither the worst single-feature inflation nor the conditioning of the design as a whole approaches the level at which coefficient variances would be materially unstable, so individual coefficient magnitudes may be read with ordinary care rather than treated as unidentified.Validation nonetheless notes as a standing caveat that the billing-and-repayment features move together, and that a re-specification which drops or adds one of them should be expected to redistribute weight across the others even though the present diagnostics are within tolerance.### Stability across declared regimesThis subject does not carry a declared regime partition, so the regime-by-regime stability comparison is outside the scope of what applies to this model type.It is listed in Appendix D among the checks that do not apply, and no regime-partitioned result should be read into this section.### Rate-shock scenariosThe rate-shock battery is scoped to hazard models, and this subject is not one, so the value change at the extreme shocks, the monotonicity of the shock curve, and the convexity of that curve against a declared direction do not apply.These three are likewise listed in Appendix D as not applicable to this model type, and the absence of shock results in this section reflects that scoping rather than an inconclusive test.### AssessmentOn the evidence that applies to this model type, the sensitivity picture is confined to the multicollinearity diagnostics, and both of them clear their thresholds with margin.Nothing in this section is raised for the findings section.
judge_rationale: All five hold; every numeral cited correctly, no names or missing-number claims.

answer: Design was assessed as documentation and developmental evidence for the model's construction and key modeling choices, using interpretability measures and benchmarking against an alternative model where theoretical review alone would not settle the question [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].The champion is a logistic regression on credit-bureau and account-history inputs, fitted on 3500 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#n_train]] training rows with an intercept of -1.396 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#intercept]], scoring 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]] in AUC and 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]] in Brier score on test.The declared inventory holds 12 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#n]] features, of which 2 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#at_origination]] are known at origination and 10 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#before_period_start]] are known before the performance period starts.None are timed inside the performance period, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#during_period]], and none are timed after the outcome is known, 0 [[art:abbb748e:run.features#after_outcome]], so on timing alone every input is observable at scoring time.The developer's own collinearity screen dropped inputs whose variance inflation exceeded a threshold of 10 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#vif_threshold]].The most recent bill amount was removed at a variance inflation of 160.9 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.bill_last.vif]] and the six-month mean utilisation at 36.36 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#removed.utilisation_mean_6m.vif]].Both removals are defensible on their face, since each near-duplicates information already expressed by a retained level or ratio term, and the screen is applied before fitting rather than chosen after seeing performance.The largest fitted coefficient by magnitude is on the most recent delinquency status at 0.7334 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.delinq_last.value]], and its positive sign is what credit subject matter expects, in that a current delinquency raises default odds.Next by magnitude are the six-month mean bill amount at -0.3726 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_mean_6m.value]], the six-month mean payment ratio at -0.3554 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.pay_ratio_mean_6m.value]], utilisation at 0.2662 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.utilisation.value]] and the six-month bill trend at -0.2225 [[art:74c10f15:run.model_summary#coefficients.bill_trend_6m.value]].The negative loading on the mean payment ratio and the positive loading on utilisation both read as expected, since paying down a larger share of the balance lowers risk and running closer to the limit raises it.The negative loadings on the mean bill level and the bill trend are weaker prior expectations, but neither is perverse once the payment-ratio and utilisation terms are in the specification.The sign checks compare each fitted coefficient against the direction of that feature's own single-feature relationship with default on train, and the ablation deltas are measured from a refit of the champion's form on every retained feature scoring 0.748 [[art:3a44e438:ablation.baseline_auc]] in AUC.Across the retained set, 3 [[art:e223cd4a:sign_check.n_disagreements]] coefficients carry a sign that contradicts their feature's univariate direction, and no rule is read against these quantities, so they are recorded here as developmental evidence bearing on the design judgement.The credit limit enters with a coefficient of sign 1 [[art:6af6aef2:sign_check.limit_bal.coef_sign]] while its own univariate direction is -1 [[art:56d284d6:sign_check.limit_bal.univariate_direction]], giving agreement 0 [[art:0278aad1:sign_check.limit_bal.agrees]]; refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.0004286 [[art:63faa640:ablation.limit_bal.delta_auc]], an improvement, so the flip sits on a term the model barely uses.The most recent payment ratio enters with a coefficient of sign 1 [[art:f018263e:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of -1 [[art:f8e46d75:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.univariate_direction]], giving agreement 0 [[art:79abee77:sign_check.pay_ratio_last.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.002411 [[art:5f39089e:ablation.pay_ratio_last.delta_auc]], again upward, so it too carries no discrimination the model depends on.The six-month maximum delinquency enters with a coefficient of sign -1 [[art:a07d68ab:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.coef_sign]] against a univariate direction of 1 [[art:b9088f4a:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.univariate_direction]], giving agreement 0 [[art:c946359c:sign_check.delinq_max_6m.agrees]]; dropping it changes test AUC by 0.0003598 [[art:3a0d3a0c:ablation.delinq_max_6m.delta_auc]], the smallest of the three, so this is the least consequential of the disagreements.All three sit on features that correlate strongly with a retained neighbour, which is the ordinary reading of a sign flip in a fitted linear specification, and in each case the ablation delta says the model would not lose discrimination without the term.By contrast, the features the model actually leans on agree in sign with their univariate direction: the most recent delinquency status, agreement 1 [[art:a8ba9372:sign_check.delinq_last.agrees]], loses 0.07585 [[art:3150b111:ablation.delinq_last.delta_auc]] of test AUC when dropped, utilisation, agreement 1 [[art:d0c9a130:sign_check.utilisation.agrees]], loses 0.01977 [[art:d4ad2039:ablation.utilisation.delta_auc]], and the six-month mean bill amount, agreement 1 [[art:89279c3b:sign_check.bill_mean_6m.agrees]], loses 0.0016 [[art:3b91a889:ablation.bill_mean_6m.delta_auc]].The six-month mean payment ratio also agrees in sign, agreement 1 [[art:7e9a76ca:sign_check.pay_ratio_mean_6m.agrees]], though refitting without it changes test AUC by 0.006603 [[art:90fa1178:ablation.pay_ratio_mean_6m.delta_auc]], an improvement, so its contribution to ranking is not what its coefficient magnitude would suggest.On balance the specification's discrimination is concentrated in delinquency status and utilisation, both signed as the subject matter expects, and the sign disagreements fall on terms the model does not rely on.Effective challenge was exercised with a histogram gradient boosting challenger on the same inputs.The challenger reaches 0.824 [[art:bf5be719:challenger.auc]] in AUC against the champion's 0.748 [[art:5c6c2bfc:metrics.test.auc]], a lead of 0.07598 [[art:c9e502ae:challenger.delta_auc]], and it is also better calibrated in aggregate at a Brier score of 0.1258 [[art:f9e0583d:challenger.brier]] against 0.1489 [[art:bbe69430:metrics.test.brier]].The bound that decides whether such a gap matters is an AUC lead of 0.03 [[art:e042774c:threshold.E1.delta_auc]], and the observed lead is well past it.This is finding E1, and because the challenger draws on the same features and differs only in admitting nonlinearity and interactions, the gap is evidence about the champion's functional form rather than about its inputs or its feature timing.That finding is reported in the findings section, and the design assessment here should be read subject to it: the champion's construction is coherent and its economics read correctly, but a same-input nonlinear alternative extracts materially more discrimination from the same data.

answer: Validation of conceptual soundness calls for critical analysis of modelling choices and assumptions, weighing both the quality and the extent of the developmental evidence behind them [[reg:SR26-2:V.1.a]].The superseded guidance is cited alongside it for an expectation the current conceptual-soundness text does not restate in the same terms: that sensitivity analysis check the effect of small changes in inputs and parameter values on outputs, and that testing over a wide range of values, including extreme ones, establish the conditions under which a model may become unstable [[reg:SR11-7:V.1.a]].### Multicollinearity among the retained featuresThe largest variance inflation factor over the retained feature set is 7.295 [[art:9ae7c45b:vif.max]], against a threshold of 10 [[art:aeb4f33c:threshold.M1.vif]] applied to any retained feature.That maximum belongs to the trailing mean bill amount, at 7.295 [[art:f0a2f865:vif.bill_mean_6m]], and it sits just above the most recent payment ratio at 7.264 [[art:c2de8dfe:vif.pay_ratio_last]] and the trailing mean payment ratio at 7.259 [[art:e39c3e82:vif.pay_ratio_mean_6m]].The rest of the design is more loosely coupled: the credit limit at 4.803 [[art:ddfdcc3c:vif.limit_bal]], utilisation at 3.215 [[art:536fdb6f:vif.utilisation]], the trailing delinquency count at 2.561 [[art:38974def:vif.delinq_count_6m]], the trailing maximum delinquency at 2.408 [[art:71aaaf11:vif.delinq_max_6m]], the most recent delinquency reading at 1.412 [[art:48733638:vif.delinq_last]], the trailing bill trend at 1.201 [[art:9356a256:vif.bill_trend_6m]], and age at 1.002 [[art:74c06cad:vif.age]].The clustering of the highest values is what would be expected of billing and payment-ratio features drawn from a shared exposure signal, and it marks the region of the design where this diagnostic comes nearest to its threshold without reaching it.Coefficients on those correlated features should therefore be read as jointly rather than individually identified, even though the diagnostic passes.Belsley's condition number of the column-standardised design is 5.547 [[art:e41b9562:condition_number]], comfortably inside its threshold of 30 [[art:7e52fd7a:threshold.M1.condition_number]].The two diagnostics agree: no retained feature is close to a linear combination of the others, and the standardised design as a whole is well conditioned, so the coefficient estimates are not expected to be unstable under small perturbations of the training data.### Analyses that do not apply to this model typeThe remaining sensitivity analyses named for this section are scoped to model types other than this one, and Appendix D lists them on that basis.Stability across declared regimes is an analysis for a package that declares a regime column, and the rate-shock scenarios — the change in value at the extreme shocks, whether the shock curve is monotone, and the sign of its convexity against the direction the package declares — are analyses for a hazard model.Neither condition holds for the package under review, so nothing in this section should be read as reporting a regime comparison or a shock curve that was run.The sensitivity evidence supporting this section is accordingly the multicollinearity work above, and the guidance's expectation of input-perturbation and extreme-value testing is met here only to the extent that design conditioning speaks to it.Nothing reported in this section is carried forward as a finding.
judge_rationale: All numbers cited and matching; no bare names or missing-quantity claims.
